sides.text: Loose coupling
Components interact through queues, topics, or APIs so one can fail or scale without breaking the others

more.text: Use SQS, SNS, EventBridge, and API Gateway between tiers.

sides.text: Horizontal vs vertical scaling
Horizontal: add instances (scale out). Vertical: bigger instance (scale up)

more.text: Horizontal is preferred for resilience; vertical has an upper limit and often downtime.

sides.text: Stateless vs stateful
Stateless workloads keep no session data locally, so any instance can serve any request

more.text: Move state to ElastiCache, DynamoDB, or S3.

sides.text: Amazon SQS
Fully managed message queue; producers and consumers are decoupled

more.text: Standard: at-least-once, best-effort ordering, nearly unlimited throughput. FIFO: exactly once, ordered.

sides.text: SQS settings
Visibility timeout (default 30 s), retention 4 days (max 14), message size 256 KB, long polling reduces empty receives

more.text: Dead-letter queues capture messages that fail repeatedly.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: A consumer takes 90 seconds to process a message. What should change?

more.head: Answer
more.text: Raise the visibility timeout above 90 seconds
more.extra: Otherwise the message reappears and is processed twice

sides.text: SQS FIFO throughput
300 messages/s per API action, 3,000 with batching; high-throughput mode raises it

more.text: Message group IDs preserve order within a group.

sides.text: Amazon SNS
Pub/sub topics that push to many subscribers (SQS, Lambda, HTTP, email, SMS)

more.text: Fan-out: one SNS topic to multiple SQS queues.

sides.text: SNS + SQS fan-out
Publish once to SNS; each SQS queue receives a copy and processes independently

more.text: Durable and decoupled.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Order events must update inventory, billing, and email independently

more.head: Answer
more.text: Publish to an SNS topic with three SQS subscribers
more.extra: Each service scales and fails independently

sides.text: Amazon EventBridge
Serverless event bus routing events from AWS services, SaaS, and your apps with rules and schemas

more.text: Successor to CloudWatch Events; supports scheduling.

sides.text: AWS Step Functions
Orchestrates workflows with state machines across Lambda and other services

more.text: Standard workflows run up to a year; Express workflows are high-volume and short.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Coordinate several Lambda functions with retries and branching

more.head: Answer
more.text: Step Functions state machine

sides.text: Amazon API Gateway
Create, secure, and scale REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs; throttling, caching, auth with IAM, Cognito, or Lambda authorizers

more.text: Pairs with Lambda for serverless backends.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: Expose a Lambda function as a public REST API with throttling and API keys

more.head: Answer
more.text: API Gateway with a Lambda integration
more.extra: Usage plans enforce quotas per key

Run code without servers
scales automatically
billed per request and duration

sides.text: Lambda concurrency
Default 1,000 concurrent executions per Region; reserved concurrency guarantees capacity; provisioned concurrency removes cold starts
Event-driven architecture

more.text: Scales independently and costs less when idle.

High availability vs fault tolerance
HA: recovers quickly with minimal downtime. Fault tolerance: continues operating with no interruption despite failures

more.text: FT usually costs more.

sides.text: Multi-AZ design
Spread instances, databases, and load balancers across at least two AZs

Replicate to another Region for DR or low latency

RPO and RTO
RPO: how much data loss is tolerable. RTO: how long to restore

more.text: Lower values cost more.

sides.text: DR: backup and restore
Cheapest; RPO and RTO in hours

more.text: Back up to S3 and restore when needed.

sides.text: DR: pilot light
Core components (database replication) always on; the rest is off until needed

more.text: RTO tens of minutes.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: RTO of 30 minutes with low cost, database must be current

more.head: Answer
more.text: Pilot light: replicate the database, keep servers off until failover
more.extra: Warm standby is faster but costs more

sides.text: DR: warm standby
A scaled-down but fully functional copy runs; scale up on failover

more.text: RTO minutes.

sides.head: Example
sides.text: RTO of a few minutes; a scaled-down full copy is acceptable

more.head: Answer
more.text: Warm standby

sides.text: DR: multi-site active-active
Full capacity in two or more Regions serving traffic

more.text: Near-zero RTO and RPO, highest cost.
